summary: Eight concrete, comment-endorsed products and tools from the verified HN front-page discussion.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Saracroche
items.source_story_title: France to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls
items.summary: An open-source French call-filtering app that blocks unsolicited calls.
items.why_included: Multiple commenters reported sustained success blocking spam calls for themselves and family.
items.evidence: A French user warmly recommends it after two months of family use, and a reply reports no spam calls since installation.

evidence_sources.author: ducdetronquito
evidence_sources.excerpt: It’s free, open source, all my family uses it for about 2 months now and it just works.

evidence_sources.author: RockstarSprain
evidence_sources.excerpt: Great app, had no spam calls going through since installing it.

items.name: Hister
items.source_story_title: As AI eats the web, the internet’s collective memory is disappearing
items.summary: A private search engine for visited pages and local files, with MCP access.
items.why_included: It directly addresses the thread’s concern that useful pages disappear or become hard to retrieve.
items.evidence: A commenter surfaces Hister as a personal archive that indexes full page and file contents for later retrieval.

evidence_sources.author: swed420
evidence_sources.excerpt: Hister is a private search engine for the pages you visit and the files you keep.

items.name: uBlacklist
items.source_story_title: As AI eats the web, the internet’s collective memory is disappearing
items.summary: A browser extension for blocking unwanted sites from search results.
items.why_included: The endorsement is unusually concrete: it made web search bearable again for the commenter.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends uBlacklist as their practical response to poor-quality search results.

evidence_sources.author: duskdozer
evidence_sources.excerpt: ublacklist is the only thing that makes searching bearable for me now.

items.name: Stowaway
items.source_story_title: Stowaway – Take the window seat on any plane or satellite overhead
items.summary: A live-feeling visual ride-along from aircraft and satellite viewpoints.
items.why_included: The project earned clear praise for turning live flight and satellite data into a distinctive exploratory experience.
items.evidence: Commenters praised both its surprising concept and the sensory details of the experience.

evidence_sources.author: vintagedave
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love this: the sound effects oddly are what really make it.

evidence_sources.author: stevage
evidence_sources.excerpt: Pretty amazing. One of those great sites that is just "wow, I would never have thought of trying to build that".

items.name: LFM2.5 2.6B
items.source_story_title: LFM2.5 2.6B model competitive with 4x larger models
items.summary: A 2.6B-parameter local model aimed at lightweight agentic and extraction workloads.
items.why_included: It has concrete evidence of useful local speed on unusually old hardware, alongside a case for intentionally small-model design.
items.evidence: One commenter reports 25–30 tokens per second on a 2013 Mac Pro, while another highlights Liquid AI’s focus on reliable tiny models.

evidence_sources.author: h14h
evidence_sources.excerpt: the official 6-bit quant of 2.6B runs at 25-30 tok/s under llama.cpp on one of the D500 GPUs.

evidence_sources.author: 0xbadcafebee
evidence_sources.excerpt: They target reliable operation of tiny models in ways other model families don't

items.name: MiniMax H3
items.source_story_title: H3-metal – Native MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon
items.summary: An open-weights video model with a native Apple Silicon inference implementation.
items.why_included: First-hand local use and strong enthusiasm make it a notable option for Apple Silicon video experimentation.
items.evidence: A MacBook Pro owner says the model works extremely well through ComfyUI, while another commenter calls the open-weights release disruptive.

evidence_sources.author: Meleagris
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using MiniMax H3 on my M5 Pro 64GB MacBook Pro through ComfyUI. It works extremely well.

evidence_sources.author: Art9681
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's a VERY disruptive model in all the good ways.

items.name: Git-knife
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Git-knife – Edit commit messages, authors, and dates like a spreadsheet
items.summary: A spreadsheet-like interface for rewriting Git commit messages, authors, and dates.
items.why_included: The thread gives concrete maintenance cases where a visual history editor is genuinely useful.
items.evidence: Commenters cite correcting mistaken author identity and reconstructing accurate archival commit dates as real uses.

evidence_sources.author: f1shy
evidence_sources.excerpt: Many times I had a wrong configured terminal and messed up the author.

evidence_sources.author: simonw
evidence_sources.excerpt: Sometimes I do a scraping project where I want the commit dates to match when the data actually changed

items.name: Jolt
items.source_story_title: Jolt: Clojure compiler implemented with Chez Scheme
items.summary: A Clojure implementation on Chez Scheme for self-contained native applications.
items.why_included: It has an explicit early report of successfully building small standalone applications across macOS and Linux.
items.evidence: A commenter tested it successfully for small self-contained apps and reports macOS and Linux support.

evidence_sources.author: mark_l_watson
evidence_sources.excerpt: works great to build small self contained apps.
